# Testing in Host Apps

Extraction, MCP servers, and console tooling require a booted Rails environment. Three host apps are available for validation — pick based on the scenario.

| Environment | Path | Purpose | Rails | DB | Docker? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **woods-testbed** (rails-8.0) | `~/lost-in-the/woods-testbed/apps/rails-8.0` | Primary — Rails 8 sample app for day-to-day validation, smoke scripts, MCP/ERD/console testing | 8.0 | SQLite | Yes (`woods-testbed-rails-8.0` container) |
| **woods-testbed** (rails-7.2) | `~/lost-in-the/woods-testbed/apps/rails-7.2` | Parity variant — same shape as rails-8.0, pinned to Rails 7.2 for cross-version coverage | 7.2 | SQLite | Yes (`woods-testbed-rails-7.2` container) |
| **test_app** | `~/work/test_app` | Integration specs with committed fixtures (`spec/integration/`) | 8.1 | SQLite | No |
| **compose-dev/admin** | `~/work/compose-dev/admin` | Production-shaped MySQL app for real-world stress cases | — | MySQL | Yes (`bc_admin` container) |

**Gem mounting:**
- `woods-testbed` (both variants): bind-mounted at `/woods-gem` inside each container. Default source is `../woods` relative to the testbed repo; override with `WOODS_GEM_PATH=/path/to/woods-worktree` when bringing the variant up.
- `test_app`: `gem "woods", path: "~/lost-in-the/woods"` in its Gemfile.
- `admin`: volume-mounted at `/gems/woods` via `docker-compose.override.yml`.

Changes to the gem are reflected immediately in all host apps without reinstalling.

**Validation via agents:** for anything beyond a quick one-command check, spawn an agent with a clear plan. Don't run long multi-step integration workflows directly from the gem session.

## woods-testbed Validation (default)

**Repository:** [`lost-in-the/woods-testbed`](https://github.com/lost-in-the/woods-testbed) — clone alongside the woods gem (sibling directories).

**Working directories:** `~/lost-in-the/woods-testbed/apps/rails-8.0` and `~/lost-in-the/woods-testbed/apps/rails-7.2`.

**Containers:** `woods-testbed-rails-8.0` and `woods-testbed-rails-7.2` — assumed to be running when needed. Verify with `docker ps | grep woods-testbed` before any command; if a variant isn't up, bring it up from the testbed repo root:

```bash
cd ~/lost-in-the/woods-testbed
docker compose up -d rails-8.0    # or rails-7.2
```

**Gem mount inside each container:** `/woods-gem` (read-only). **App mount:** `/app` (read-write, bind of the per-variant app dir).

**Shared smoke scripts:** `~/lost-in-the/woods-testbed/scripts/` is mounted read-only at `/app/script/shared` inside both containers. Use paths like `script/shared/woods_smoke.rb` when invoking via `bin/rails runner`.

```bash
# Extraction (rails-8.0 — swap container name for rails-7.2)
docker exec woods-testbed-rails-8.0 bash -lc 'cd /app && bin/rails woods:extract'
docker exec woods-testbed-rails-8.0 bash -lc 'cd /app && bin/rails woods:incremental'
docker exec woods-testbed-rails-8.0 bash -lc 'cd /app && bin/rails woods:stats'
docker exec woods-testbed-rails-8.0 bash -lc 'cd /app && bin/rails woods:validate'
docker exec woods-testbed-rails-8.0 bash -lc 'cd /app && bin/rails woods:clean'

# Shared smoke scripts (canonical regression coverage)
docker exec woods-testbed-rails-8.0 bash -lc 'cd /app && bin/rails runner script/shared/woods_smoke.rb'
docker exec woods-testbed-rails-8.0 bash -lc 'cd /app && bin/rails runner script/shared/woods_credentials_smoke.rb'

# Rails 7.2 variant — same scripts, different container
docker exec woods-testbed-rails-7.2 bash -lc 'cd /app && bin/rails runner script/shared/woods_smoke.rb'

# Ad-hoc Rails runner
docker exec woods-testbed-rails-8.0 bash -lc 'cd /app && bin/rails runner "puts Woods.configuration.inspect"'

# Interactive Rails console
docker exec -it woods-testbed-rails-8.0 bash -lc 'cd /app && bin/rails console'
```

Triggers on Buildkite, bk, CI build logs, failed jobs, pipeline failures.
- dev-feedback-writeups: Generates and reviews mixed-audience dev writeups for Linear, GitHub, and similar async channels — issue comments, PR descriptions and replies, status updates, feature progress, technical updates of any kind. Use whenever drafting OR reviewing any writeup that engineers, PMs, and QAs will all read. Triggers on phrases like 'draft a Linear comment', 'write a GitHub reply', 'draft a PR description', 'post an update', 'review this draft', 'make this less dense', 'too jargon-heavy for PMs', or any time an agent is about to post technical content to a multi-audience channel. Use aggressively — dense engineer-to-engineer prose in Linear/GitHub is the default failure mode for AI-assisted dev workflows; most drafts benefit even without explicit request. For long-form documents (PRDs, RFCs, design docs), use tech-docs instead.
- double-diamond-planning: Structured double-diamond (Discover → Define → Develop → Deliver) planning for Rails features, projects, and epics, grounded in product-minded engineering and iterative small-slice delivery. Use this skill whenever the user wants to plan, scope, kick off, frame, slice, or break down any piece of development work — a new feature, a refactor, an epic, a migration, a quarterly project — or asks "how should we approach X", "help me think through X", "plan X", "scope X", or "what's the right way to build X". Also use it when the user wants to pressure-test a problem statement, explore solution options, split work into releasable increments, write a project brief, or prepare for an RFC or kickoff. Trigger even if they don't say "double diamond" or "planning" explicitly — any request that involves going from a fuzzy idea to an actionable plan qualifies.
- excalidraw: Generate architecture diagrams as .excalidraw files from codebase analysis, with optional PNG/SVG export. Use when the user asks to create architecture diagrams, system diagrams, visualize codebase structure, generate excalidraw files, export excalidraw diagrams to PNG or SVG, or convert .excalidraw files to image formats.
- fetch-markdown: This skill should be used when fetching a URL, web article, blog post, or documentation page as clean readable markdown. Triggers on requests like "fetch this URL as markdown," "get the content of this page," "read the README for X library," "what does this repo's CLAUDE.md say," "pull that article as text," or "get the agent context for this GitHub repo." Uses defuddle MCP tools (defuddle_fetch, get_readme, get_repo_context) with WebFetch fallbacks when MCP is unavailable. DO NOT use for: Notion pages (use Notion MCP tools instead), GitHub issues or pull requests (use GitHub MCP issue_read/pull_request_read instead), Linear tickets (use Linear MCP get_issue instead). ## claude.ai Linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

## rails-diff
Rails Diff MCP Server - compare Rails versions to see what changed in `rails new` output between releases. Use `list_rails_versions` to see available versions, then `compare_rails_versions` to get the file list summary, and `get_file_diff` to retrieve the patch for individual files.

## unblocked
Unblocked = institutional context behind code: PRs, design docs, chat, issues, incidents, code history, cross-repo code. Code search answers WHAT; Unblocked answers WHY, WHO, WHEN. Skipping risks duplicating rejected approaches, violating team conventions, stomping in-flight work, or missing incident context.

### Primary tool

`context_research` — semantic + relational research across docs, PRs, chat, issues, incidents, code. Use when question spans entities or needs synthesis. For a known URL, use `context_get_urls` instead — cheaper, returns fully hydrated content (supports GitHub/GitLab, Jira, Linear, Notion, Confluence, Slack, Google Docs, Asana, Coda, Sentry, Datadog, Stack Overflow Teams, Unblocked docs/threads).

### When to call context_research

Proactively. Do not wait for the user.

- Start of any planning, investigation, refactor, migration, or feature task. Fire in parallel with your first Explore/Grep/Read — zero latency cost.
- "Why does this exist" or "why done this way". Code cannot answer these.
- Behavior doesn't match the code. Check history first.
- Unfamiliar class, service, endpoint, flag, config key, or error string.
- Before writing new code. Check if the pattern, bug, fix, or helper already exists.
- Incident, alert, or outage. Connect affected systems to recent changes and fix patterns.
- Filtered activity lookups ("PRs merged last week in auth", "open incidents tagged ingestion").
- Before recommending a solution. Verify the approach hasn't been tried or rejected.

If unsure, call. Missed context is expensive.

### Effort

- `low` (default) — targeted lookup anchored on one entity, URL, or file.
- `medium` — exploratory, no clear anchor.
- `high` — planning, architecture, migration, incident retro, cross-system investigation. Use whenever producing a plan or design.

All Unblocked tools are read-only.

# Detects the correct admin container (main or agent stack) and launches
# the index server inside it.

set -euo pipefail

INDEX_DIR="/app/tmp/woods"

# Claude Code passes literal "${AGENT_SLOT}" when the env var is unset.

  CONTAINER="bc_admin_agent_${SLOT}"

else
  CONTAINER="bc_admin"
fi

  exit 1

# metadata) `search` loads; the gem default of 500 silently misses most of a

- [ ] A second consecutive scheduled run reports ~0 synced (manifest hit, not a cold re-push).

* Cadence revisit (separate from the restore): with steady state ≈ 0, per-merge syncing becomes viable and gives fresher review profiles than nightly.

{"id":"ENG-5480","title":"Restore Woods incremental extraction across CI runs (build-time savings)","description":"## Problem / Context

Every scheduled Woods CI run extracts the *entire* app from scratch (~6,559 units), which is the bulk of the woods step's compute and wall-time. woods supports incremental extraction (`woods:incremental`): given a stored `dependency_graph.json` + the previous SHA, it re-extracts only the units changed since the last run. Restoring that graph across CI runs — the same plumbing as the sync-manifest restore (<issue id="a311cd9b-6663-4d25-bcb7-01c09e44c81d" href="https://linear.app/bigcartel/issue/ENG-5462/restore-woods-sync-manifest-across-ci-runs-revisit-cadence">ENG-5462</issue>) — would cut extraction time and compute substantially. Parent: <issue id="0201c23a-2030-4988-aaa4-2240d403cc70" href="https://linear.app/bigcartel/issue/ENG-5434/improve-unblocked-code-reviews">ENG-5434</issue>.

## Why this matters

Extraction is the slowest part of the scheduled build and grows with the codebase. At per-merge cadence (the direction <issue id="a311cd9b-6663-4d25-bcb7-01c09e44c81d" href="https://linear.app/bigcartel/issue/ENG-5462/restore-woods-sync-manifest-across-ci-runs-revisit-cadence">ENG-5462</issue> opens up), a full cold extract on every merge is wasteful; incremental extraction keeps the step cheap as both frequency and codebase size grow.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The woods-extract step restores `dependency_graph.json` from the last successful scheduled build before extracting.
- [ ] Extraction runs incrementally — only units changed since the restored SHA are re-extracted.
- [ ] When no graph restores, the step falls back to a full extract (no failure).
- [ ] Extraction wall-time on an unchanged/lightly-changed run drops measurably vs a cold extract.

## Notes / Limitations

* **Lower priority than the sync-manifest restore (**<issue id="a311cd9b-6663-4d25-bcb7-01c09e44c81d" href="https://linear.app/bigcartel/issue/ENG-5462/restore-woods-sync-manifest-across-ci-runs-revisit-cadence">ENG-5462</issue>**).** Now that `woods:unblocked_sync` skips unchanged docs, incremental extraction only saves extraction *minutes* — it does not reduce Unblocked API calls. <issue id="a311cd9b-6663-4d25-bcb7-01c09e44c81d" href="https://linear.app/bigcartel/issue/ENG-5462/restore-woods-sync-manifest-across-ci-runs-revisit-cadence">ENG-5462</issue> is the budget win; this is the compute/time win.
* **Shares** <issue id="a311cd9b-6663-4d25-bcb7-01c09e44c81d" href="https://linear.app/bigcartel/issue/ENG-5462/restore-woods-sync-manifest-across-ci-runs-revisit-cadence">ENG-5462</issue>**'s dependency:** persisting + restoring an artifact across builds needs the Buildkite API token (or S3 cache plugin), and `dependency_graph.json` must be added to the step's `artifact_paths`.
* Best sequenced *after* <issue id="a311cd9b-6663-4d25-bcb7-01c09e44c81d" href="https://linear.app/bigcartel/issue/ENG-5462/restore-woods-sync-manifest-across-ci-runs-revisit-cadence">ENG-5462</issue> lands the restore plumbing — this rides on it.","priority":{"value":0,"name":"No priority"},"url":"https://linear.app/bigcartel/issue/ENG-5480/restore-woods-incremental-extraction-across-ci-runs-build-time-savings","gitBranchName":"eng-5480-restore-woods-incremental-extraction-across-ci-runs-build","createdAt":"2026-06-30T17:52:19.083Z","updatedAt":"2026-06-30T17:52:19.083Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"slaType":"all","status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":[],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"f8ca8a23-c5d8-4545-998f-eaa78dd0f349","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-06-30T17:52:19.083Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Leah Armstrong","createdById":"e897e765-9d8f-42f8-942a-7858122ea323","project":"AI Idea Backlog","projectId":"bd132fe9-5806-4118-8010-91079fbec51a","parentId":"ENG-5434","team":"Engineering","teamId":"7e868d2d-b32d-459a-9a61-ec3b40b0d2da"}

=== woods-review-solutions.md ===
# Catching PR concerns sooner with Woods — solution options

> Grounded in the ENG-5434 evaluation (see `eng5434-woods-eval-draft.md`). Core finding: **Unblocked won't consume Woods** — automated review has no collection access; PR Chat can't be scoped and isn't retrieving it (proven via the Account probe: gave ~70 forward assocs + "no structural-profile database", not the 340 reverse-dependents); only Q&A/Slack presets can be pointed at a collection. **So stop trying to make Unblocked pull Woods — push Woods' authoritative data to the PR instead.**

**Stack reality:** admin CI is **Buildkite** (not GitHub Actions). `UNBLOCKED_API_TOKEN` is already on the SLC agents. `gh` is available in CI. The Woods index (`dependency_graph.json` with `file_map`, `reverse`, `pagerank`) is already produced by `woods:extract`.

## Options

### 1. Woods-native blast-radius Buildkite step → PR comment  ★ RECOMMENDED PRIMARY
A PR-build pipeline step, gated on changed paths (`app/models/`, `app/services/`, `db/migrate/`, GraphQL), that maps the PR's changed files → units (via `file_map`) → their **reverse-dependents + PageRank + entry points + callback side-effects** (from `reverse`/`pagerank`), and posts a structured PR comment via `gh`.
- **Pros:** delivers Woods' **authoritative, complete** data (the 340-dependents / PageRank #1 that source-reading *and* Unblocked undercount). Deterministic, no LLM hallucination, no retrieval gamble, no Unblocked dependency. Fits existing Buildkite + agent-env.
- **Cons / needs:** a thin Woods feature — `woods:pr_blast_radius CHANGED=<files>` (rake/CLI/MCP) — though `file_map`+`reverse`+`pagerank` are all already in the artifact, so it's a small addition (you own Woods). Requires the `dependency_graph.json` available on PR builds (restore the last main artifact — ties to ENG-5462's restore plumbing — or extract). Raw report, not prose (arguably a feature).
- **Verdict:** the surest path — uses Woods' strength directly, sidesteps every Unblocked limitation.

### 2. Unblocked CLI `context-research` Buildkite step → PR comment  ◐ CONDITIONAL COMPLEMENT
Pipeline step runs `unblocked context-research "<content-framed Woods prompt>"` and posts the result. The CLI uses the Q&A pipeline, which *can* reach connected collections.
- **Pros:** LLM synthesis (readable, prioritized); if Woods is retrievable, blends Woods + PR history + docs.
- **Cons:** **UNPROVEN for Woods** — in this eval, `context_research` (same Q&A pipeline) returned **source-level** answers (Account "~7–10", not 340), i.e. it has the *same* connection/discoverability dependency as PR Chat. Needs the collection actually connected to the Q&A pipeline **+** the two discoverability issues (preamble, dependent-names) **+** possibly a Data Source Preset scoped to Woods. Can hallucinate (the documented semantic false-positives). Needs a PAT secret in CI.
- **Verdict:** only viable *after* confirming the Q&A pipeline surfaces Woods (re-run the Account probe via the CLI). If it works, layer synthesis on top of Option 1's raw data — not a reliable standalone.

### 3. Slack auto-answer scoped to a Woods Data Source Preset  ◐ DEV Q&A, NOT A PR GATE
Slack channels *do* support Data Source Presets (unlike PR Chat), so a channel can be scoped to Woods.
- **Pros:** the one interactive Unblocked surface you *can* point at Woods; good for ad-hoc "blast radius of X?" dev questions.
- **Cons:** not tied to PRs; dev-initiated; routing an answer back to a PR is clunky. Doesn't catch concerns automatically.
- **Verdict:** secondary — a Woods-scoped dev Q&A channel, not a PR-review gate.

### 4. Local `woods-admin` MCP / `querying-codebase-structure` skill (ENG-5461)  ★ COMPLEMENT (shift-left)
Developers/their agents query the Woods MCP while authoring/reviewing — the proven-strong surface (340 dependents on demand).
- **Pros:** Woods' definitively-working surface; catches concerns at *authoring* time (earliest possible); already built.
- **Cons:** manual/adoption-dependent; not automatic per-PR.
- **Verdict:** the best "shift-left" lever; pairs with Option 1's automated safety net.

### 5. Keep Unblocked automated review + notes/`AGENTS.md`  — BASELINE (non-Woods)
Unblocked's automated review is already strong from source (caught the #13895 defect on a thorough pass). Its real weakness is *semantic false positives* — fixed by the reply-text-mined notes + `AGENTS.md` rules (harvester deliverable). Orthogonal to Woods; worth doing regardless.

## Recommendation

1. **Build Option 1** — a Buildkite PR-build step emitting Woods' blast-radius report for changed model/service/migration units, posted as a PR comment. It's the only path that reliably delivers the data Woods uniquely has, and it needs just a thin `woods:pr_blast_radius` feature + the index available on PR builds.
2. **Pair with Option 4** (local MCP) to catch concerns at authoring time.
3. **Keep Option 5** (automated review + notes/AGENTS.md) as the general-purpose reviewer; it doesn't need Woods.
4. **Option 2 only if** a CLI re-probe proves the Q&A pipeline surfaces Woods (then it adds synthesis); **Option 3** as an optional dev Q&A channel.

**Through-line:** flip the architecture — **Woods produces the blast-radius report, Buildkite posts it.** That uses Woods' strength (authoritative graph) and CI's strength (deterministic PR gate), and stops depending on an Unblocked surface that can't reach the collection.

---

# Meeting brief (2026-07-02) — insights + recommendation

## What Woods uniquely provides (proven)
Complete structural blast radius that source-reading undercounts: **Account 340 dependents / PageRank #1 of 6,813**; **Oauth::Client 41** (incl. 3 Support::Dev controllers + Integrations::ZapierController); **ProductOption 46**. Source-reading / Unblocked consistently gave "~7–10." This exhaustive reverse-dependency + entry-point + PageRank data is Woods' irreplaceable contribution.

## Why Unblocked's surfaces struggle to consume it
- **Automated review:** no custom-collection access at all (architectural).
- **PR Chat:** no data-source scoping; empirically doesn't retrieve Woods (probe returned forward assocs + "no structural-profile database").
- **CLI `context-research`:** **scoped token DOES retrieve Woods profiles** (proven — `Oauth::Client (model)` / `Account (model)` appeared in sources; a *broad* token dilutes them under code). BUT (a) it's a **retrieval tool, not a reasoner** — empty on "what could break" analytical queries; and (b) the profiles list dependents by **count, not name** (+ no preamble), so even when retrieved they don't carry the reverse-dependent names. Needs doc fixes (issues #1/#2).

## The through-line: the bug-catcher = capable agent + complete structure
Neither half alone works — Woods is inert data; a diff-only reviewer undercounts structure; a retrieval tool can't reason. The catch requires an **agent that reasons over the diff AND has the complete structure.**

## Recommendation for the Hermes decision
**Integrate Woods with Hermes via the Woods MCP** (`dependents`/`lookup`/blast-radius). This is the strongest architecture the whole eval points to:
- Hermes supplies the **reasoning** (what context-research can't).
- The Woods MCP supplies **complete structure directly** — no token-scoping, no discoverability tuning, no retrieval gamble (the MCP returned the full 340/41 cleanly every time).
- It's the in-house version of "Claude + Woods MCP + diff," which was the one path that reliably combined reasoning + complete structure.

**Fallback (free, fiddly):** Buildkite → `context-research` with a Woods-scoped token → PR comment, *after* shipping doc-fix issues #1/#2. Viable, but context-research's weak reasoning caps its value.

**Deterministic floor:** the Woods-native blast-radius CI step (spike works) — a no-agent attention checklist, no "may break" judgment.

## Woods index lifecycle for per-PR review — findings

### 1. Incremental mechanics & cost (`extract_changed`, `extractor.rb:289–326`)
**Inputs it needs:**
- A prior **`dependency_graph.json`** in the output dir (`extractor.rb:291–292`). It's loaded via `DependencyGraph.from_h`. **No prior graph → empty graph → `affected_by` returns nothing → zero units re-extracted.** The graph is mandatory, not optional.
- A **changed-files list**, resolved by `woods.rake:56–73` in priority order: `CHANGED_FILES` env → `CI_COMMIT_BEFORE_SHA` (GitLab) → `GITHUB_BASE_REF` (`git diff origin/base...HEAD`) → `git diff HEAD~1`. No stored SHA of its own — it derives the diff from env/git each run. Files are filtered to a relevant-path allowlist (`woods.rake:76–98`: models, controllers, services, jobs, migrations, `schema.rb`, `routes.rb`, `Gemfile.lock`, etc.).

**What it re-extracts:** directly-changed units **+ their transitive dependents** (BFS over reverse edges, unbounded depth — `dependency_graph.rb:65–86`). Each affected unit is re-run through its extractor and rewritten; affected type `_index.json`s regenerated.

**Rails boot still required — YES.** `extract_changed` calls `safe_eager_load!` (`extractor.rb:297`) exactly like full extraction. The boot + `eager_load!` is a fixed floor both modes pay.

**Cost vs full:** The **Rails boot + eager-load dominates** for a large app and is *identical* in both modes. Incremental only saves the extractor-scan pass + git enrichment (`git log` over all files). So on a ~6,500-unit app incremental saves extraction *minutes*, not the boot. This matches ENG-5480's own framing ("saves extraction time, not API calls").

**⚠️ Two correctness caveats I confirmed:**
- **Incremental misses newly-added files.** `affected_by` seeds from `@file_map[f]` (`dependency_graph.rb:66`); a file not already in the (main) graph isn't found, so a PR that *adds* a model/service is silently not extracted. Same for renames (old identifier lingers, new one absent).
- **`extract_changed` skips `resolve_dependents` and `write_graph_analysis`** (both only run in `extract_all`, lines 246/270). It *does* recompute PageRank at write time (`:724`), but **`graph_analysis.json` goes stale** after an incremental run (hubs/orphans/cycles not refreshed).

### 2. Recommended freshness strategy — **the latest `main` graph is good enough; do NOT re-index the PR branch**
The reviewer's core question is *"what depends on the changed units"* — i.e. **reverse-dependents + PageRank**. Those reverse edges are a whole-codebase property that lives almost entirely in `main` and is highly stable (e.g. `Account` = 340 dependents / PageRank #1). A PR changes a unit's *forward* deps, not the set of things that depend on it. **So map the PR's changed files → units (via `file_map`) → reverse-dependents + PageRank from the restored main graph.**

**When a stale main graph misleads (call these out in the report, don't re-index for them):**
- PR **adds** a unit → absent from main's graph (no node, no `file_map` entry).
- PR **renames/moves** a unit → old identifier's dependents shown, new one missing.
- PR **deletes** a depended-on unit → dependents still listed (that's actually the useful signal: "you're removing something 40 things depend on").
- New **forward** edge added by the PR (changed file now calls X) → not in main graph, but this is secondary for blast-radius.

### 3. Recommended iterative-push handling (PR pushed 10×/day) — **stable main graph + per-push file-diff; never re-extract per push**
Re-extraction (full *or* incremental) pays a Rails boot every push — far too expensive for 10 pushes. Instead:
- **Restore the last main `dependency_graph.json` once** (ENG-5462/5480 restore plumbing) and treat it as read-only.
- **Per push, only recompute the changed-file list** and re-run the (cheap, no-boot, deterministic) file→unit→reverse-dependents+pagerank query.
- **Debounce:** trigger on a settled push (Buildkite `concurrency_group` + cancel-superseded so push #7 doesn't post while #8 is in flight).
- **Comment idempotency:** maintain **one sticky PR comment** (find-and-update by a hidden marker via `gh`), not 10 new ones. Optionally diff against the last posted blast-radius and only re-post/flag when the changed-unit set actually changes — most pushes touch the same files.

Cost tradeoff: this is ~seconds of graph lookup per push vs minutes of boot+extract. The only thing you lose by not re-indexing is picking up brand-new units the PR adds — acceptable, and detectable (a changed file with no `file_map` hit → flag "new unit, no blast-radius data yet").

### 4. How the reviewer should consume it — **agent + MCP-by-name is the strongest; deterministic report is the floor**
The eval (`woods-review-solutions.md`, ENG-5434) is decisive here:
- **Best: an agent (Hermes / Claude) that reasons over the diff + queries the `woods-admin` MCP by unit name** (`dependents`/`lookup`/`pagerank`). The MCP returns complete structure directly with no retrieval/token-scoping gamble — it cleanly returned the full 340/41 dependents every time. Reasoning (agent) + complete structure (MCP) is the only combo that reliably catches concerns.
- **Deterministic floor: a Woods-native blast-radius CI step** that maps changed files → reverse-dependents+PageRank and posts a structured `gh` PR comment. No LLM, no hallucination — an "attention checklist," not a judgment.
- Unblocked's automated-review and PR-Chat surfaces **cannot consume Woods** (no collection access / no scoping — proven), so don't route through them.

### 5. New Woods capability needed
- **A `woods:pr_blast_radius CHANGED=<files>` task/CLI/MCP tool does NOT exist yet** (confirmed — no `blast_radius` entrypoint in `lib/`/`exe/`). It's a thin addition: `file_map` + `reverse` + `pagerank` are all already in the artifact; it just needs to map changed paths → units → reverse-dependents+PageRank+entry-points and emit a report. This is the single missing piece for both the deterministic floor and to feed the agent.
- **Nice-to-have:** a "new/renamed unit" detector (changed file with no `file_map` hit) so the report flags PR-added units that the stale main graph can't cover.
- Cross-run artifact persistence (restore `dependency_graph.json`) is exactly **ENG-5480**, riding on **ENG-5462**'s Buildkite restore plumbing — no new Woods code, just CI wiring.

## Woods index lifecycle for per-PR review — findings

### 1. Incremental mechanics & cost (`extract_changed`, `extractor.rb:289–326`)
**Inputs it needs:**
- A prior **`dependency_graph.json`** in the output dir (`extractor.rb:291–292`). It's loaded via `DependencyGraph.from_h`. **No prior graph → empty graph → `affected_by` returns nothing → zero units re-extracted.** The graph is mandatory, not optional.
- A **changed-files list**, resolved by `woods.rake:56–73` in priority order: `CHANGED_FILES` env → `CI_COMMIT_BEFORE_SHA` (GitLab) → `GITHUB_BASE_REF` (`git diff origin/base...HEAD`) → `git diff HEAD~1`. No stored SHA of its own — it derives the diff from env/git each run. Files are filtered to a relevant-path allowlist (`woods.rake:76–98`: models, controllers, services, jobs, migrations, `schema.rb`, `routes.rb`, `Gemfile.lock`, etc.).

**What it re-extracts:** directly-changed units **+ their transitive dependents** (BFS over reverse edges, unbounded depth — `dependency_graph.rb:65–86`). Each affected unit is re-run through its extractor and rewritten; affected type `_index.json`s regenerated.

**Rails boot still required — YES.** `extract_changed` calls `safe_eager_load!` (`extractor.rb:297`) exactly like full extraction. The boot + `eager_load!` is a fixed floor both modes pay.

**Cost vs full:** The **Rails boot + eager-load dominates** for a large app and is *identical* in both modes. Incremental only saves the extractor-scan pass + git enrichment (`git log` over all files). So on a ~6,500-unit app incremental saves extraction *minutes*, not the boot. This matches ENG-5480's own framing ("saves extraction time, not API calls").

**⚠️ Two correctness caveats I confirmed:**
- **Incremental misses newly-added files.** `affected_by` seeds from `@file_map[f]` (`dependency_graph.rb:66`); a file not already in the (main) graph isn't found, so a PR that *adds* a model/service is silently not extracted. Same for renames (old identifier lingers, new one absent).
- **`extract_changed` skips `resolve_dependents` and `write_graph_analysis`** (both only run in `extract_all`, lines 246/270). It *does* recompute PageRank at write time (`:724`), but **`graph_analysis.json` goes stale** after an incremental run (hubs/orphans/cycles not refreshed).

### 2. Recommended freshness strategy — **the latest `main` graph is good enough; do NOT re-index the PR branch**
The reviewer's core question is *"what depends on the changed units"* — i.e. **reverse-dependents + PageRank**. Those reverse edges are a whole-codebase property that lives almost entirely in `main` and is highly stable (e.g. `Account` = 340 dependents / PageRank #1). A PR changes a unit's *forward* deps, not the set of things that depend on it. **So map the PR's changed files → units (via `file_map`) → reverse-dependents + PageRank from the restored main graph.**

**When a stale main graph misleads (call these out in the report, don't re-index for them):**
- PR **adds** a unit → absent from main's graph (no node, no `file_map` entry).
- PR **renames/moves** a unit → old identifier's dependents shown, new one missing.
- PR **deletes** a depended-on unit → dependents still listed (that's actually the useful signal: "you're removing something 40 things depend on").
- New **forward** edge added by the PR (changed file now calls X) → not in main graph, but this is secondary for blast-radius.

### 3. Recommended iterative-push handling (PR pushed 10×/day) — **stable main graph + per-push file-diff; never re-extract per push**
Re-extraction (full *or* incremental) pays a Rails boot every push — far too expensive for 10 pushes. Instead:
- **Restore the last main `dependency_graph.json` once** (ENG-5462/5480 restore plumbing) and treat it as read-only.
- **Per push, only recompute the changed-file list** and re-run the (cheap, no-boot, deterministic) file→unit→reverse-dependents+pagerank query.
- **Debounce:** trigger on a settled push (Buildkite `concurrency_group` + cancel-superseded so push #7 doesn't post while #8 is in flight).
- **Comment idempotency:** maintain **one sticky PR comment** (find-and-update by a hidden marker via `gh`), not 10 new ones. Optionally diff against the last posted blast-radius and only re-post/flag when the changed-unit set actually changes — most pushes touch the same files.

Cost tradeoff: this is ~seconds of graph lookup per push vs minutes of boot+extract. The only thing you lose by not re-indexing is picking up brand-new units the PR adds — acceptable, and detectable (a changed file with no `file_map` hit → flag "new unit, no blast-radius data yet").

### 4. How the reviewer should consume it — **agent + MCP-by-name is the strongest; deterministic report is the floor**
The eval (`woods-review-solutions.md`, ENG-5434) is decisive here:
- **Best: an agent (Hermes / Claude) that reasons over the diff + queries the `woods-admin` MCP by unit name** (`dependents`/`lookup`/`pagerank`). The MCP returns complete structure directly with no retrieval/token-scoping gamble — it cleanly returned the full 340/41 dependents every time. Reasoning (agent) + complete structure (MCP) is the only combo that reliably catches concerns.
- **Deterministic floor: a Woods-native blast-radius CI step** that maps changed files → reverse-dependents+PageRank and posts a structured `gh` PR comment. No LLM, no hallucination — an "attention checklist," not a judgment.
- Unblocked's automated-review and PR-Chat surfaces **cannot consume Woods** (no collection access / no scoping — proven), so don't route through them.

### 5. New Woods capability needed
- **A `woods:pr_blast_radius CHANGED=<files>` task/CLI/MCP tool does NOT exist yet** (confirmed — no `blast_radius` entrypoint in `lib/`/`exe/`). It's a thin addition: `file_map` + `reverse` + `pagerank` are all already in the artifact; it just needs to map changed paths → units → reverse-dependents+PageRank+entry-points and emit a report. This is the single missing piece for both the deterministic floor and to feed the agent.
- **Nice-to-have:** a "new/renamed unit" detector (changed file with no `file_map` hit) so the report flags PR-added units that the stale main graph can't cover.
- Cross-run artifact persistence (restore `dependency_graph.json`) is exactly **ENG-5480**, riding on **ENG-5462**'s Buildkite restore plumbing — no new Woods code, just CI wiring.
